### 10.2.1 The compiled column, and how it was measured

The compiled column of the gates that moved into `harbor-gates` was
measured with the same harness (`bench/gates/measure.sh`, the `maxrss`
parent) on the same tree, with the TWO VARIANTS INTERLEAVED: one python
run, one binary run, twelve times each, and the MINIMUM of each.

The interleaving is the point. The box is shared, and its load drifts over
minutes — a batch measurement of the python column and a batch measurement
of the binary column land in different weather, and the difference between
them is then the weather. Interleaving puts both variants under the same
load, and the minimum of each is the least foreign work each variant had
to do.

| gate | python (s) | the binary (s) | RSS python | RSS the binary |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `check-string-switch.py` | 3.424 | 1.621 | 18.1 MB | 11.6 MB |
| `check-string-switch-report.py` | 3.451 | 1.534 | 18.1 MB | 11.6 MB |
| `check-result-chains.py` | 4.171 | 0.744 | 18.3 MB | 19.1 MB |
| `check-md-links.py` | 1.005 | 1.048 | 20.4 MB | 17.0 MB |
| `md-lint.py` | 0.654 | 0.132 | 19.3 MB | 10.4 MB |
| `check-arch-anchors.py` | 0.659 | 0.088 | 17.2 MB | 10.1 MB |
| `check-arch-suite-once.py` | 0.190 | 0.024 | 17.5 MB | 7.9 MB |
| `guard-triage.py` | 1.218 | 0.501 | 30.6 MB | 15.4 MB |

Six of the eight are two to eight times faster. The two that are not are
the two whose cost is not python:

* **`check-md-links.py` is a wash** (1.005 s against 1.048 s). The gate
  reads 398 documents and matches 1428 links in them, and both
  implementations spend that on the same two things: the regular
  expression that finds a link and the file reads. The port paid for
  RE2's slower scan with a cheaper pattern — dropping the optional `!`
  from the link pattern gives RE2 the `[` as a literal prefix, and that
  one change is 446 ms to 35 ms over the tracked markdown.
* **`check-result-chains.py` uses MORE resident memory** as a binary
  (19.1 MB against 18.3 MB). The census keeps every guard site of the
  tree in memory, and the Go runtime maps more of the heap than the
  interpreter does for the same data.

The python column of the MAIN table above is an older measurement, taken
on another machine, and the two columns of a row are therefore not from
one moment. The table of this section is the one to compare: same tree,
same moment, same box, both variants interleaved.

**The reflection-JSON row was measured on its own, and here is its
provenance.** The table above is one snapshot: the same harness, the same
tree, the same moment. The port of this gate (#2122) landed after that
snapshot, so its number was measured separately, with the same harness
(`bench/gates/measure.sh`, `RUNS=5`, the minimum wall time kept) on the tree
of the port, the python gate measured before its original was deleted and the
compiled gate after. Four rounds of five runs each, because this host is
shared:

| | python | compiled |
|---|---:|---:|
| the wall time, the best round | 0.714 s | 0.194 s |
| the spread of the four rounds | 0.714-0.965 s | 0.194-0.339 s |
| the peak RSS | 17 796-17 808 KB | 14 500-16 588 KB |

The gate scans `tests/**/*.cs` and the scan is the whole of its work, so the
two numbers are the same work measured twice: **3.7x** faster as a binary on
the best round of each. The set's sum falls by the difference of the two
best rounds, 0.520 s; the sum was not re-measured, and a sum that mixes two
snapshots is not a number, only the delta is.


Three numbers, and they are the whole answer to "what does the language
buy":

1. **The set cost 619 s**, and 547 s of it was ONE gate. The other 28
   instruments together cost 72 s.
2. **The git batching takes the set from 619 s to 117 s (5.3x)**, and it
   touches no language at all.
3. **The compiled gates take the set from 117 s to 117 s**, because the two
   gates that moved are the ones that were cheap: the seam graph is 1.6 %
   of the set.

A single gate's speed-up is not the set's speed-up. The seam graph is
**16.5x** faster as a binary (15.9 s to 1.0 s), and that is worth 2.4 %
of the set. The doc-cites gate is 88 % of the set, and its cost is git
processes, not python: 414 of its 547 seconds are inside `git`.

**What the full port would be worth, and what it would not.** If every
gate were compiled, the set would be bounded by the doc-cites gate's
python scanning: about 55 s of scanning and 13 s of git. The full port is
therefore worth roughly 619 s to 60 s, and the batching is worth 619 s to
117 s on its own.

Since then the port landed: twenty-six gates are compiled, and the set is
measured again in §10.2. The 117 s of that table is the set of 28 gates on
the tree of that day; the set of 43 gates on commit `be078f5a` costs
25.644 s on a runner (§10.2), and the two numbers differ by the gates that
were not in the old set at all, by the language mix, by the tree and by the
machine.

## 10.3 One command for the tree: `harbor-gates all`

**The question.** One binary, one command, no dotnet and no python: run every
gate that needs nothing but the tree and print one verdict. Issue #2135 asks
for this. The command is already in the tree: it landed with the work recorded
under #2122, it is registered in `tools/gates/main.go`, its list lives in
`tools/gates/all/gates.go`, `docs.yml` runs it in the `tree gates` job, and
`tools/check-local.sh` calls it on a developer machine.

**What it runs.** The list has 26 gates. The command starts the gates that are
compiled into the binary and reports the rest without starting them: a gate
that is still a python script needs a workflow of its own, because the binary
must not need python. On the measured tree that is 16 compiled gates, 9 python
gates and one writer (`normalize-mtimes`, which rewrites the tree and so cannot
be part of a check). The self-test, `harbor-gates all --self-test`, proves that
a red gate gives exit 1 and names itself, that a gate that cannot start gives
exit 2, that the report order does not depend on the order gates finish, and
that the list names only gates a workflow runs with nothing that the build
produces.

**The number.** CI run `44035166979` (`docs.yml`, 2026-11-17, ubuntu-26.04,
tree at `3f79e00f`) spent **17 s** on the `tree gates` job: 11 s in checkout,
**3 s** in the step that runs `harbor-gates all`, and the rest in setup. The
report printed 16 gates with exit 0 and a sum of gate times of **7.493 s**.
The slowest compiled gates were `check-test-projects` at 2.216 s,
`check-local-merge-loss` at 1.894 s and `check-abstractions-contract` at
934 ms. The 3 s step is under the 25 s budget the issue sets.

The 9 python gates are not in that number: they run in their own `docs.yml`
jobs. `check-doc-cites`, the gate the issue calls out as taking 68 s to 120 s,
is one of them. The split answers the open question in the issue without a
speed-up to that gate: the compiled command is fast because the expensive gate
stays python and runs elsewhere, and `tools/check-local.sh` still runs the
python gates on a local machine. A reader who wants full tree coverage in one
local call runs that script, not the binary alone.

Reproduce the number with `gh run view 44035166979 --log` and filter for
`tree gates`.

## 11. What a pull request costs

**The question this section answers.** Three numbers about the pull-request
lane were known, and none of them was the price of a pull request:

* issue [#2108](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/issues/2108)
  measured the bill of ONE lane run: 19.4 runner-minutes, 17 jobs, run
  `39556560488`;
* issue [#2110](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/issues/2110)
  measured what CLOSES the lane (the arch shard);
* §10 measured the gate set, on a runner, one gate at a time.

What nobody had was the whole bill: the runner-minutes, the wall, the
critical path and the peak width of one pull request, and the split of that
bill by what the seconds buy. A decision about the lane needs all four,
because they are four different numbers and only one of them is a sum.

**THE INSTRUMENT.** `tools/gates/pr-cost` is a compiled gate, the same binary
the repository already ships (`tools/bin/harbor-gates-linux-x64 pr-cost`).
It reads what the Actions REST API returns and prints the tables below; its
input is the job list of a run, so no number in this section was transcribed
by hand. It is REPORTING: it never fails a build. Its own proof that it can
fail is its `--self-test`, which plants a stripe whose wall, busy time and
peak width are known, and a timestamp that cannot be parsed (that one must
be an ERROR, because an unreadable timestamp read as "no time" would report
a bill of zero, and zero is the number that looks like good news).

### 11.1 The sample, and what it is

Twelve pull requests, the last twelve of 2026-10-21 that built the tree and
ran the five test shards, 16:47:08 to 17:22:51 UTC. The criterion is
mechanical and is in the data: the `build` job of `ci.yml` ran, all five
shards ran, and every job of both workflows finished. A pull request that
touches only `docs/` or only `tools/` never starts the .NET build: its bill
is 4.8 runner-minutes, and it is a different shape, not a cheaper pull
request.

| | |
|---|---|
| the twelve runs | `39637885344`, `39638416505`, `39638565635`, `39638603945`, `39638705616`, `39639468264`, `39640369150`, `39640971168`, `39641227183`, `39641476017`, `39641977262`, `39643272476` |
| their head commits | `eee6a5b1`, `f7257f8d`, `6d47858e`, `90e1c345`, `9c4853d7`, `938ae03c`, `f25f2075`, `372d0285`, `b854599b`, `dbd9f9a0`, `a828bed6`, `222fa198` |
| their `docs.yml` twins | the runs started in the same second on the same branch |
| the workflows | `ci.yml` (13-14 live jobs) and `docs.yml` (21 live jobs; 22 on the one branch that adds the `workflow files` gate) |
| the pool | `ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm` |
| dev's tip that day | `13961b71` and `bb9c76b9` (dev moved twice inside the sample window) |

**WHICH ATTEMPT THE TABLES READ.** Four of the twelve had a flaky shard and
were re-run. Every table in this section reads the FIRST attempt of each run,
because that is one pass of the lane, and a second pass is a separate bill
(§11.2 names its price). The Actions API serves the LAST attempt by default
(`filter=latest`), and for those four runs the two differ: the re-run
replaces the failed job's timestamps with later ones, so the default view is
a mixture of two attempts, and its wall is 393 to 745 s longer. Reading the
first attempt needs `filter=all` and a pick of the lowest `run_attempt`
(§11.8).

**THE TREE THE TWELVE RAN ON, AND WHAT CHANGED IN THE LANE SINCE.** The
`ci.yml` of all twelve heads has the SAME job list as dev's `ci.yml` today:
the same thirteen jobs, in the same order, and the `reference-trimmer` job is
still in it. Four things changed inside the lane since:

| change | what it does to the pull-request lane |
|---|---|
| [#2123](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/pull/2123) | three `DIAGNOSTIC` steps in the `build` job. They run only when the build-output cache matched, and it never matched in the twelve, so they cost 0 s there and 7 s in the run of 2026-10-22 below |
| [#2134](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/pull/2134) | the `aot-publish` job's gate is the compiled binary now, not the python script. Same job, same lane |
| [#2153](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/pull/2153) | the ILLink analyzer and the vs-threading family leave the ordinary build: 801.3 analyzer-seconds become 491.4, the change's own measurement. Its WALL effect was inside the 28 s noise floor of the harness that measured it, so the compile is cheaper by an amount the harness could not resolve |
| [#2155](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/pull/2155), [#2158](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/pull/2158) | `MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1` in the `build` job, and `HarborArchGate: 'false'` for every event. The pull-request lane already had the architecture gate off, so the second half of that change does not touch it |

Two more changed the lane's shape since, one of them still in flight. The
`go-quality` gate of PR #2162 joined the `docs.yml` gate lane: that lane
runs twenty-two jobs today, and the sample's twenty-one had no such job. The
unused-reference analyzer moves into the ordinary compile in PR #2138, and
the `reference-trimmer` job is deleted with it. That pull request is not
merged yet: the job is still in dev's `ci.yml`, and §11.6 measures the
lane it will produce.

**THE WALL IS NOT THE SUM, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** `ci.yml` and `docs.yml`
have no `needs:` between them, so they start together, and the pull request
waits for the LONGER of the two. The bill is their sum and the wall is
their maximum. A table that adds the two columns to get the wall is wrong,
and the wrongness is the expensive kind: it says every new job costs the
whole wall.

### 11.2 What one pull request costs

| pull request | runs | jobs | runner-min | wall (s) | critical path (s) | peak width | busy (s) | idle (s) | mean concurrency | the tail |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PR #39637885344 (feat/workflow-parse-gate) | 2 | 35 | **23.4** | 787 | 787 | 5 | 626 | 161 | 1.78 | `gate` |
| PR #39638416505 (test/1812-e2e-framework) | 2 | 35 | **23.8** | 796 | 796 | 5 | 582 | 214 | 1.79 | `gate` |
| PR #39638565635 (test/1553-ensure-guards) | 2 | 35 | **27.1** | 718 | 718 | 6 | 578 | 140 | 2.27 | `gate` |
| PR #39638603945 (feat/gates-a) | 2 | 34 | **23.5** | 1018 | 1018 | 4 | 707 | 311 | 1.38 | `gate` |
| PR #39638705616 (fix/ci-duplicate-yaml-key) | 2 | 34 | **23.4** | 724 | 724 | 5 | 640 | 84 | 1.94 | `gate` |
| PR #39639468264 (refactor/1569-testkit-scaffold) | 2 | 35 | **25.4** | 962 | 962 | 6 | 667 | 295 | 1.58 | `gate` |
| PR #39640369150 (refactor/1569-testkit-scaffold-b) | 2 | 35 | **24.1** | 832 | 832 | 6 | 582 | 250 | 1.74 | `gate` |
| PR #39640971168 (feat/gates-d-3) | 2 | 34 | **22.7** | 790 | 790 | 5 | 663 | 127 | 1.73 | `gate` |
| PR #39641227183 (feat/2111-msbuild-switches) | 2 | 34 | **23.1** | 983 | 983 | 6 | 641 | 342 | 1.41 | `gate` |
| PR #39641476017 (feat/gates-a) | 2 | 34 | **21.9** | 915 | 915 | 5 | 635 | 280 | 1.44 | `gate` |
| PR #39641977262 (arch/1724-semantic-guards) | 2 | 34 | **23.5** | 925 | 925 | 6 | 632 | 293 | 1.52 | `gate` |
| PR #39643272476 (feat/gates-d-3) | 2 | 34 | **21.2** | 742 | 742 | 5 | 599 | 143 | 1.72 | `gate` |

**THE HEADLINE.** A pull request in this repository costs **23.5
runner-minutes** (median; min 21.2, max 27.1) and **814 s of wall**
(median; min 718, max 1018). The critical path is the wall by definition,
from the first job's start to the last job's end, and it is always the
`gate` job that ends it.

**THE FOUR THAT NEEDED A SECOND ATTEMPT.** The re-run is a second pass of
the lane, and it is not in the tables above. Its price is WALL, not runner
time: the re-run replaces the failed shard's seconds with a new shard's
seconds, so the bill barely moves, and what it adds is the wait for a runner
and for the lane to be checked again.

| pull request | the shard that failed | first attempt: wall / runner-min | last attempt: wall / runner-min | the re-run costs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PR #39639468264 | `test (ui)` | 962 s / 25.4 | 1355 s / 25.4 | 393 s of wall, 0.0 runner-min |
| PR #39640369150 | `test (ui)` | 832 s / 24.1 | 1573 s / 24.1 | 741 s of wall, 0.0 runner-min |
| PR #39641227183 | `test (core)` | 983 s / 23.1 | 1728 s / 23.0 | 745 s of wall, 0.1 runner-min |
| PR #39641476017 | `test (platform)` | 915 s / 21.9 | 1306 s / 22.1 | 391 s of wall, 0.2 runner-min |

**THE ANCHOR RUN, READ BY THE SAME INSTRUMENT.** Issue #2108's number,
19.4 runner-minutes and 17 jobs, is the `ci.yml` LANE of run `39556560488`,
and the instrument reads it back exactly: ci.yml 19.4 runner-minutes over
13 live jobs (the 17 are the jobs the lane declares; four of them were
skipped). The WHOLE stripe of that run, ci.yml plus its `docs.yml` twin, is
**23.0 runner-minutes** and 909 s of wall, against the twelve's median 23.5
and 814 s, and the decomposition agrees with the twelve to within a point
per article: build 29 % against 25 %, reference trim 19 % against 19 %, test
shards 26 % against 27 %, docs gates 15 % against 16 %. The reference run
and the twelve are the same lane.

**THE TWO WORKFLOWS, SEPARATELY.** The median `ci.yml` lane is 19.3
runner-minutes over 13 jobs; the median `docs.yml` lane is 3.8
runner-minutes over 21 jobs. The `docs.yml` lane is 16 % of the bill and it
is ENTIRELY off the critical path: in all twelve runs the `ci.yml` lane is
the longer one, so the gate lane never set the wall. It starts with
`ci.yml`, runs its twenty-one gates in parallel, and finishes long before
the build does.

| pull request | workflow | jobs | runner-min | wall (s) | wait before the first job (s) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| PR #39637885344 | docs.yml | 22 | 4.0 | 407 | 15 |

### 11.3 The bill, article by article

The twelve pull requests together: **283.1 runner-minutes**.

| article | runner-min | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| build (compile) | 69.4 | **25 %** |
| build (reference trim) | 53.9 | **19 %** |
| test shards | 75.2 | **27 %** |
| docs.yml gates | 46.3 | **16 %** |
| packaging | 18.1 | 6 % |
| ci.yml gates | 13.8 | 5 % |
| aot publish | 3.6 | 1 % |
| orchestration (`changes`, `gate`) | 2.5 | 1 % |
| **total** | **283.1** | **100 %** |

**THE TWO FULL BUILDS ARE A THIRD OF THE BILL.** The `build` job compiles the
tree once (median 250 s of compile); the `unused references
(ReferenceTrimmer)` job compiles it AGAIN, from scratch, in its own job
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml:726`), and its own median wall is 274 s. Two
full compiles per pull request: 470 s of the 1410 s of a median pull
request's bill, **33 %**, and the two jobs' own walls (358 s and 274 s) are
632 s of the `ci.yml` lane's 1158 s, **55 % of the lane**, and 45 % of the
whole stripe's bill. Issue #2108 measured the same two builds as 660 s and
44 % of the bill on run `39556560488`; the shape is unchanged, and the share
grew because the gate lane got cheaper around it.

**THE BUILD JOB, STEP BY STEP** (median of the twelve; the job's own wall is
358 s, min 291, max 392):

| step | seconds |
|---|---:|
| **NUKE compile (Release, zero warnings, docs, deterministic)** | **250** (min 184, max 273) |
| setup .NET 10 (+ the NuGet cache) | 26 |
| stash the pack inputs (the `pack` job's slice) | 20 |
| stash the build outputs, core and ui shards | 10 each |
| checkout | 8 |
| the TUnit-analyzer and installer gates | 2 each |

**The ReferenceTrimmer job** (median wall 274 s): its own `dotnet build` is
**220 s** (min 161, max 265), the restore with the analyzer is 11 s, setup
.NET is 32 s.

**THE SHARDS** (median wall): `test (arch)` **124 s** (min 86, max 148),
`test (ui)` 78 s, `test (core)` 68 s, `test (platform)` 64 s, `test (e2e)`
46 s. The `pack` job's own wall is 90 s. The arch shard is the LONGEST of
the five in 12 of the 12 runs, and the last one to FINISH in 7 of the 12,
which is what issue #2110's reading of the lane's tail is confirmed by: the
lane's tail is a shard.

**THE CRITICAL PATH, STAGE BY STAGE** (median): `changes` to `build` to
shards to `gate` = **725 s** (min 640, max 883). The `gate` job itself is
2 to 4 s of work; it waits a median of **95 s** for a runner after the last
shard ends (min 32 s, max 213 s), because it is the one job that can only
start when everything else has finished.

### 11.4 What each known fix is worth

| fix | what it is | runner-minutes per pull request | wall | issue |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| the ReferenceTrimmer is a second full build | merging it into the main compile, or reusing the build's outputs | **not measured as a delta.** The job is still in dev and still 19 % of the sample's bill. On the lanes of 2026-10-22 the stripe costs 19.0 runner-minutes with the job and 18.5 without it, but those are two different runs with different cache states, so the difference is not the merge's price | **0 measured** | [#2108](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/issues/2108) |
| the commit sha in `AssemblyInformationalVersion` | `IncludeSourceRevisionInInformationalVersion=false` (`Directory.Build.props:72`) | **0 on the runs of 2026-10-21, and that is now a fact about the cache, not about the fix.** The compile step of those twelve is 184 to 273 s (median 250 s), and the build-output cache did not fire: the "Restore the build outputs (obj/ + bin/)" step took 0 s in eight runs and 1 s in four, and the log of the newest of them says `Cache not found for input keys: msbuild-v1-…`. On the pull-request run of 2026-10-22 the cache DID fire (24 s of restore) and the compile took 45 s. The lever is the cache; the fix is what makes a restored tree valid | **0 measured**; 205 s of compile on the runs where the cache fires | [#2137](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/issues/2137) |
| the arch shard is ONE project | splitting `Harbor.Architecture.Tests` into 3-4 shards | **+2.5**, three more shard jobs, each with its own setup, download and teardown. It is a COST, not a saving | **≤ 46 s**, the arch shard's 124 s minus the next-longest shard's 78 s. That difference is the ceiling; a four-way split is a projection, not a measurement | [#2110](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/issues/2110) |
| the architecture gate runs twice on a dev push | switching it off inside the build, as the PR path already does | **0 on the PR lane** | **0 on the PR lane**; 132 s of the dev push's build, which #2158 has since removed | [#2114](https://github.com/refusedguy/Harbor-Harness/issues/2114) |
| the gate set | the `docs.yml` gate lane (21 gates in the sample, 22 today) and the `ci.yml` gates | **5.0** (3.8 + 1.2), 21 % of the bill | **0**, the gate lane runs in parallel with `ci.yml` | §10.2 |

**WHY THE #2108 FIX IS 19 % OF THE BILL AND 0 % OF THE WALL.** The
ReferenceTrimmer job runs in parallel with the `build` job, both need only
`changes`, and it is NOT in the `gate` job's `needs:` list
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml:3376`). The `gate` job is what the pull request
waits for, and it never waits for the trimmer. So the trimmer's 274 s are
274 s of runner time and not one second of wall. It does hold a runner of
the `ubuntu-24.04` pool for 274 s, concurrently with the build, so it is a
candidate for the queue wait below, which is a statement about the pool,
not about the job.

### 11.5 The 4 vCPU question, and the width of the lane

**The hypothesis is already falsified for the build, by measurement.**
§6.7 is the falsification: one MSBuild node is not slower than four
(ratio 1.02 on the wall, 0.95 without the architecture gate), because a
SINGLE compilation already uses 3.3 to 3.6 of the runner's four cores,
Roslyn's parallel analyzer driver inside one `CoreCompile`. More MSBuild
nodes buy nothing; more CORES do.

**What this section adds is the width of the lane itself.** The peak width
of the twelve pull requests is **4 to 6 jobs** (median 5), and the mean
concurrency over the wall is **1.38 to 2.27** (median 1.72). The lane is
not short of parallelism at its peak: the burst after the build runs the
`pack` job and five shards at once, on three runner pools.

**AND THE RUNNERS ARE NOT IDLE BECAUSE THE LANE HAS TOO FEW JOBS, THEY ARE
IDLE BECAUSE THE POOL IS QUEUED.** The idle column of §11.2 is the time the
pull request spent with NO job running: a median of **232 s of the 814 s
wall (29 %)**. That is the queue wait, and the queue is the repository's own
load: during the measured window **11 to 32 `ci.yml` and `docs.yml` runs
were in flight at once (median 20)**, against 0 to 5 (median 1) in the hour
around the runs of 2026-10-22 below. A pull request in this repository is
queued behind the merge train, and the wall is a property of the
repository's throughput, not of the lane's shape.

**SO WHAT IS THE LEVER.** Not "more parallel jobs in the lane": the lane
already fans out to six after the build, and the runner is not waiting for a
job. The two levers that the measurements point at are:

1. **the compile, on a second runner**, 250 s of the 358 s build job, and
   the build is on the critical path. §6.7 estimates ~1.4x for two
   independent clusters of the project graph, and this measurement says the
   term is 250 s of a 725 s chain;
2. **the queue**, which is not a lane property: the wall is 29 % queue, and
   §6.9's three paired runs are the same finding from the other side.

### 11.6 The same measurement on the tree of 2026-10-22

The twelve are a measurement of 2026-10-21. The lane has moved since, and
the two pull-request runs of 2026-10-22 are the same instrument read on the
tree of today. Both are pull-request runs, and the first one ran the
`ci.yml` of dev's tip as it stands now.

| pull request | tree | ci.yml jobs | ci.yml runner-min | docs.yml runner-min | the whole stripe | wall (s) | idle (s) | peak width |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PR #39719039714 (feat/2111-msbuild-switches) | dev's `ci.yml` of 2026-10-22 | 13 | 15.8 | 3.2 | **19.0** | 326 | 2 | 13 |
| PR #39718825965 (ci/2108-merge-reference-trimmer) | the same lane with the `reference-trimmer` job removed (PR #2138) | 13 | 15.0 | 3.5 | **18.5** | 472 | 5 | 16 |

**WHAT MOVED.** The stripe's bill went from the sample's 23.5
runner-minutes to 19.0, and the bill of the PR lane of 2026-10-22 splits
this way: build (compile) 3.0 runner-min (16 %), build (reference trim) 4.2
(22 %), packaging 1.6 (8 %), test shards 6.1 (32 %), ci.yml gates 0.6 (3 %),
docs.yml gates 3.2 (17 %), orchestration 0.2 (1 %). Two things moved, and
they are not the same thing:

* **the compile.** On the run of 2026-10-22 the build-output cache FIRED
  (24 s of restore) and the compile took 45 s against the sample's 250 s.
  On the run of PR #2138's lane it did not fire and the compile took 208 s.
  The cache is the lever, and it fires on some pull-request runs and not on
  others;
* **the queue.** The idle time of the two runs is 2 s and 5 s, against the
  sample's 232 s, and the repository had 0 to 5 `ci.yml` and `docs.yml` runs
  in flight at once (median 1) against the sample's median 20. The wall of
  326 s and 472 s is a wall with no queue in it, and it is not comparable
  with the sample's 814 s as a price of the lane: the lane's own work was
  324 s and 467 s, against the sample's median 634 s.

**THE PR #2138 LANE, AS MEASURED.** The `reference-trimmer` job is gone and
the analyzer runs inside the ordinary compile. The stripe bills 18.5
runner-minutes against 19.0 with the job, and the "build (reference trim)"
article is 0. The difference between the two runs is NOT the merge's price:
the compile was 208 s in one and 45 s in the other, because the cache fired
in one and not in the other. A paired measurement of that merge is still
missing.

**THE DEV-PUSH LANE, FOR THE RECORD.** The same measurement on the push to
dev of run `39717885532` (dev's tip `a019e928`, 2026-10-22 03:37 UTC) reads
16 live ci.yml jobs, 24.8 runner-minutes and 509 s of wall, with the
compile at 183 s and the trimmer's own build at 207 s. It is the push lane
and not the pull-request lane: it saves the build outputs after the compile
and it resolves the build-output cache from the previous commit, so its
compile is not the pull-request lane's compile.

### 11.7 What this section does NOT measure

* **The nightly lane and the dev-push lane.** Both are measured elsewhere
  (§6.8 for the coverage lane); the numbers here are the pull-request lane
  only. The architecture suite does not run inside the build on any lane any
  more: `HarborArchGate` is `'false'` for every event since #2158
  (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:887`), so the 132 s that #2114 measured on a
  dev push is gone from the dev push as well.
* **The pull request that does not build.** A pull request that touches only
  `docs/` or only `tools/` never starts the .NET build; its bill is 4.8
  runner-minutes (measured on run `39641146271`, the same day) and its wall
  is 542 s of gate lane. This section's own pull request is one of them:
  PR #2169 touches no `src/`, `apps/` or `tests/` file, and its own run
  `39722580870` billed 4.5 runner-minutes over 27 jobs and a 38 s wall,
  which is five ci.yml jobs and the 22-job gate lane.
* **The cost of the queue wait.** The idle time is measured; the share of
  it that belongs to a given job is not.
* **A pull request whose build fails.** The lane then runs fewer jobs (the
  shards never start): measured on run `39639464986`, whose ci.yml lane ran
  eight jobs and 16.7 runner-minutes, and whose whole stripe is 21.5
  runner-minutes and a 1053 s wall, of which 167 s is queue.
* **The runner speed.** The spread of the compile step across the twelve
  runs (184 to 273 s) is the runner's, not the tree's; §6.4 says the same
  about the lane's own numbers.
* **The price of PR #2138.** Two lanes, two runs, two cache states. The
  merge's own price is not measured here.

### 11.8 How to reproduce this section

```bash
# One file per pull request: the runs of BOTH workflows, as the API reports
# them. `filter=all` returns the jobs of EVERY attempt, and the first attempt
# is the one this section reads: the lowest `run_attempt` of the run.
stripe () {                             # $1 = run id, $2 = workflow name
  local id="$1" wf="$2" created
  created=$(gh api "repos/:owner/:repo/actions/runs/$1" --jq .created_at)
  gh api "repos/:owner/:repo/actions/runs/$1/jobs?per_page=100&filter=all" \
    | jq -s --argjson id "$1" --arg wf "$wf" --arg created "$created" \
        '([.[].jobs[]] | map(.run_attempt) | min) as $first
         | {id:$id, workflow:$wf, created_at:$created,
            jobs: [.[].jobs[] | select(.run_attempt == $first)]}'
}
{ stripe "$CI_RUN" ci; stripe "$DOCS_RUN" docs; } | jq -s '.' > run-$PR.json

# the instrument
tools/bin/harbor-gates-linux-x64 pr-cost run-*.json
tools/bin/harbor-gates-linux-x64 pr-cost --steps run-*.json   # step by step
tools/bin/harbor-gates-linux-x64 pr-cost --self-test            # the proof
```

**WHY THE FILTER IS PART OF THE RECIPE.** The Actions API serves the LAST
attempt of a run by default (`filter=latest`), and for the four runs of
§11.2 that needed a second attempt the last attempt is a mixture: the jobs
that were not re-run keep their first-attempt timestamps, and the re-run
jobs carry later ones. Dropping `--filter=all` and the pick of the lowest
`run_attempt` moves the wall of those four runs by 393 to 745 s, and the
median wall of the twelve with them.

**WHY THE RECIPE PUTS BOTH RUNS IN ONE FILE.** A pull request's bill is the
STRIPE of its two workflows, and the instrument's per-pull-request table is
a table of stripes: a file with the `ci.yml` run alone measures the lane,
and a file with both measures the pull request. The `created_at` of the run
is what the "wait before the first job" column reads, so the recipe fetches
it from the run itself.

## 12. How to reproduce

All numbers in this doc are reproducible from the repo:

```bash
# Install .NET 10
wget https://dot.net/v1/dotnet-install.sh && ./dotnet-install.sh --channel 10.0

# Clone & restore
cd /path/to/harbor
export PATH="$HOME/.dotnet:$PATH"
dotnet restore

# Build
dotnet build -c Release

# Binary sizes
ls -lh apps/Harbor.App.Cli/bin/Release/net10.0/Harbor.App.Cli.dll
du -sh apps/Harbor.App.Cli/bin/Release/net10.0/

# Cold start (median of 3 runs)
for i in 1 2 3; do
  start=$(date +%s%N)
  dotnet run --no-build -c Release --project apps/Harbor.App.Cli -- --version >/dev/null
  end=$(date +%s%N)
  echo "Run $i: $(( (end - start) / 1000000 )) ms"
done

# Microbenchmarks
dotnet run -c Release --project tests/Harbor.Benchmarks -- --filter '*'

# Tests (per project as plain executables — never `dotnet test`, see §6.2)
dotnet build -c Release
dotnet run --project tests/Harbor.Core.Tests -c Release --no-build -- --minimum-expected-tests 1
```

# Roadmap

> Harbor development roadmap. Last updated: 2026-08-27 (post CE-5 / PROD-UI-0 sprints and the
> DOCS-ZERO docs pass; autonomous sprint-chain infra lives in [`.kilo-docs/`](./.kilo-docs/) —
> `sprint-chain.md` queue + `scripts/sprint-chain.sh` dispatcher, HEAD 3625e8e).
> See [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) for the per-release change history.
>
> **Sprint-2 note:** optional UI/scripting components moved to [`contrib/`](../contrib/)
> (`contrib/tui/`, `contrib/apps/`, `contrib/scripting/`, `contrib/tests/`; build via
> `contrib/Contrib.slnx`). They still exist and work — just outside `Harbor.slnx`.

## Current State: v0.4.0-alpha → post-CE-5 (2026-08-27)

### ✅ Completed — Core

- **Architecture**: Clean/Hexagonal/Onion layering enforced via analyzers
- **TEA state machine** (`UiStore` + `AppReducer` + `AppMsg`): Elm-style unidirectional data flow
- **EventBus**: pub/sub decoupling between agent loop and UI
- **Result<T>**: Railway Oriented Programming throughout, no exceptions for expected failures
- **Zero unsafe code**: 100% safe, no `unsafe` blocks
- **NativeAOT-ready**: core can be AOT-compiled (TUI runs JIT separately)

### ✅ Completed — Providers (4 native + 13 JSON)

- Native: `Anthropic` (cache_control, extended thinking), `OpenAI` (Chat + Responses API for o1/o3), `Ollama` (local NDJSON), `OpenAiCompatible`
- JSON: OpenRouter, Kilo Code (with **FREE** models), DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral, xAI, Together, Fireworks, Cerebras, vLLM, + all OpenAI-compat

### ✅ Completed — Storage (3 backends)

- `Jsonl` (default, zero deps, append-only, atomic writes, parsed-message cache) — **decomposed in R31** (codec extracted)
- `Memory` (tests)
- `Sqlite` (indexed queries)

### ✅ Completed — UI (2 apps in `apps/` + TUI projects in src/ + optional contrib components)

- **TUI (in `Harbor.slnx`)**: `Harbor.Terminal.Abstractions` (contracts) +
  `Harbor.Tui.AnsiPlain` (ids `plain`, `ansi`), `Harbor.Tui.CellForge` (+`.Engine`,
  `.Syntax`, `.Prompts`; id `cellforge`, legacy alias `consoleex`; alt-screen
  cell-diff MVP, CE-0…CE-5), `Harbor.Tui.Notifications`. The SharpConsoleUI
  renderer (`Harbor.Tui.NickConsoleEx`, id `nickconsoleex`) is **not** in this
  list any more: it moved to `contrib/` (ADR-019), so `HARBOR_TUI=nickconsoleex`
  selects nothing.
- **TUI (optional, `contrib/tui/`, NOT in the default build)**: Spectre,
  Spectre.Fullscreen, SpectreTui, TerminalGui, Termina, RazorConsole, Sixel —
  compiled in only with `HarborWithSpectreTui=true` (see `src/Harbor.Hosting/Harbor.Hosting.csproj`;
  the CLI-side ItemGroup is commented out). The *requested* default TUI id is
  still `spectre-tui` (`TuiModule`), so in default builds it falls back loudly
  to `plain` with a warning naming the available ids — `spectre-tui` is effective

- **Web**: Blazor Server (`contrib/apps/Harbor.App.Blazor`)

### ✅ Completed — ConsoleEx MVP (CE-0…CE-5)

Second render path for the interactive REPL (`src/Harbor.Tui.CellForge/`, opt-in only):

- **Rendering** (CE-1): `ScreenBuffer` → `DiffEngine` cell-diff frames through `AnsiWriter` (SGR automaton, cursor elision, DECSYNC wrapper); resize policy à la ratatui
- **Widgets** (CE-2/3): virtualized chat timeline with byte-budget ring, streaming markdown with pacer-gated reveal, tool-call cards with unified-diff bodies, status segment bar + tick-driven spinner, multi-line composer

See [README](../src/Harbor.Tui.CellForge/README.md).
- **PTY hardening** (CE-5): `PtyHarness` runs the real process in a pseudo-terminal (`tests/Harbor.Tui.CellForge.PtyTests/`, 8 scenarios — launch/submit/kitty/mouse/paste/resize/Ctrl+C/termios); fixed Termios struct size 49→60 bytes (kernel wrote past struct → stack corruption in raw-mode Enter, commit 1749841).

## 📋 Roadmap — by version

### v0.5.0 — Plugin System & Sub-agents

> **Статус (обновлено 2026-08-27):** plugin-половина вехи выполнена раньше плана —
> декомпозирована в 8 проектов `Harbor.Plugins.*` в спринтах F/ROP-D (см. ✅ Completed
> выше и git log за 24–26.08). Sub-agent execution по-прежнему НЕ реализован.

**Plugin loading** *(выполнено, механизм отличается от исходного плана)*
- [x] Plugin host: `Harbor.Plugins.Hosting` (`PluginHost`, `PluginHostBuilder`) + out-of-process host `Harbor.Plugins.Host` (exe, MCP stdio server). Исходный план «AssemblyLoadContext (JIT mode)» заменён Roslyn CS-source pipeline: `Harbor.Plugins.Runtime/CsPluginLoader.cs` компилирует `.cs` из `~/.harbor/plugins/` in-memory; DLL-based путь остался только у legacy сэмплов
- [x] Plugin discovery from `~/.harbor/plugins/*.cs` (+ embedded-resource / in-memory / composite sources) — `Harbor.Plugins.Storage/FileSystemPluginSource.cs` et al.
- [x] Plugin trust prompt for project-local plugins — `IPluginTrustPolicy` + `TrustingPluginSource` fail-closed gate, `FileTrustPolicy` persist store path+sha256 (`~/.harbor/plugins/trust.json`, re-approval after edit), interactive y/N at startup; global scope implicitly trusted
- [x] Hot-reload via `FileSystemWatcher` — `DebouncedPluginWatcher` (generational debounce, last-event-wins) → `PluginReloadService` re-runs the startup pipeline into live registries; `/plugins reload` in REPL + auto-reload gated by `tooling.autoReloadPlugins`; edited/removed plugins still need a restart to fully rebind (unregister tracking is follow-up)
- [x] `harbor plugin install/list/uninstall` CLI commands
- [x] Agent-facing plugin management with a per-change approval gate (#1738) — the `plugin_manager` tool reads the plugin inventory (one `IPluginInventory` shared with the `/plugins` panel) and PROPOSES install/uninstall/enable/disable; the change happens only after the user approves that one call, and the approval never changes the session's permission mode
- [x] Build flag default: plain `dotnet build` now defines `HarborWithPlugins=true` (root `Directory.Build.props`) — previously the whole pipeline was dead code outside orchestrator builds ("Feature flags: plugins=False")

**Sub-agent execution** *(частично: TaskTool валидирует sub-agent, но не запускает его — `src/Harbor.Tools.Builtin/Tools/Task/TaskTool.cs`: «does NOT run it yet… execution fails with an explicit "not implemented" error»)*
- [x] Wire `TaskTool` to agent registry — Tool внедряет `IAgentRegistry`, проверяет `IsSubAgent` (G4)
- [ ] Real sub-agent runner: sub-agent runs in isolated context with own session
- [ ] Result returned to parent agent as tool output
- [ ] Support `explore`, `plan`, custom sub-agents

**TUI plugins**
- [x] `ITuiPlugin` — контракт существует, но это **закрытый шов (#564)**: `RegisterTui`
      не имеет ни одного call site в продукте, а дверь хоста `RegisterTuiPlugin` с #916
      ничего не сохраняет (её нечитаемый список `TuiPlugins` удалён)
- [x] Панельная ось (единственная живая) — `ITuiPanelPlugin` →
      `IPluginLoadHost.RegisterPanelProvider` → адаптер `Harbor.Plugins.Registration/PanelRegistryPluginAdapter.cs`
- [ ] Sample TUI plugin (e.g. token usage chart)
- [ ] Plugin views override builtin views

### v0.6.0 — MCP Integration

### v0.7.0 — Skills & LSP

**Skills**
- [x] `SKILL.md` format with YAML frontmatter (`name:`/`description:`, `<name>/SKILL.md` preferred, flat `<name>.md` legacy)
- [x] Discovery from `~/.harbor/skills/` and `.harbor/skills/` (`WorkspaceContextSource`, project shadows global)
- [x] `skill` tool to load skill content (`SkillTool`: name-only lookup, scope filter, 12k cap, path-confinement)
- [x] `<available_skills>` XML in system prompt
- [x] `harbor skill install/list` CLI commands (`SkillsCommand`: list/install/uninstall, project+global scopes)

**LSP Integration**
- [x] LSP client (own stdio JSON-RPC implementation, no NuGet — `LspManager`/`LspClient`/`LspServerSession` in `src/Harbor.Lsp/`, AOT-safe source-gen wire format)
- [x] 11 builtin language servers (TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C#, C/C++ via clangd, Java via jdtls, HTML/CSS/JSON via vscode-*-language-server, Lua)
- [x] Auto-spawn on file open (`LspManager` lazy sessions + `read` tool opens files, `edit` pushes changes)
- [x] `diagnostics`, `references`, `definition` tools (`lsp` tool, registered when `ILspService` present; graceful degradation with explanatory results when a binary is missing)
- [x] LSP-aware `read`/`edit` (reads auto-open supported files; edits notify + append a diagnostics summary line)

### v0.8.0 — Session Management Polish

- [x] Session branching (`harbor sessions fork <message-id>`) — `SessionForkRunner` copies history inclusive of the cut point into a NEW session (lineage via `ParentSessionId`, `(fork)` title); source untouched
- [x] `/tree` slash-command for branch navigation (`SessionTreeRunner`: REPL `/tree` + `harbor sessions tree`, forest by `ParentSessionId`, marks current, orphans/cycles handled)
- [ ] Branch summaries (LLM-generated on branch switch) — DEFERRED: fork creates a NEW session with no explicit "switch" moment in code (the user just continues in the new id); generating an LLM summary at fork time would add latency+cost to a local op and `SessionForkService` is deliberately store-generic with no provider wiring. Revisit when explicit branch-switch UX lands; long histories are already covered by `CompactionService` anchored summaries
- [x] Snapshot/revert (`harbor sessions revert <message-id>`)
- [x] Session search (`harbor sessions search <query>`)
- [x] JSONL import/export (`harbor sessions export/import` via `ISessionPorter`)
- [x] Session rename (`harbor sessions rename` via `ISessionStore.UpdateAsync`)
- [x] Reactive context-overflow recovery (#1755) — the provider's "context length exceeded" is classified as `ProviderErrorKind.ContextOverflow` (from the error BODY, not the status code), the history is compacted FORCED and the SAME request is retried from the compacted view, bounded by `CompactionBehavior.MaxOverflowRetries`. A compaction that frees nothing keeps the original refusal, and the run reports why it could not continue.

### v0.9.0 — Two-Process Architecture

- [ ] Core (NativeAOT) + TUI (JIT) in separate processes
- [ ] NDJSON over Unix Domain Socket wire protocol
- [ ] Late-attach with scrollback replay
- [ ] Multi-client support (terminal + IDE + web)
- [ ] `harbor serve` for headless mode
- [ ] `harbor tui` to attach to running core

### v1.0.0 — Stabilization & Polish

- [ ] API freeze for `Harbor.Abstractions`
- [ ] NuGet packages published for all `Harbor.*` libraries
- [ ] Comprehensive docs site (MdDocs / DocFX)
- [ ] Performance benchmarks vs baseline
- [ ] Security audit
- [ ] Accessibility audit (WCAG 2.1 AA for Blazor/Avalonia)
- [ ] Internationalization (i18n) for UI strings (slice 1 landed: inventory in `docs/I18N_STRING_INVENTORY.md`, catalogue home decided in ADR-015; ~1 370 occurrences pending extraction; locales + fallback tests are separate slices)

### Architectural debt

- [x] **The vendored SharpConsoleUI renderer is out of the product (ADR-019).**
  `Harbor.Tui.NickConsoleEx` (id `nickconsoleex`) and the vendored
  `nickprotop/ConsoleEx` submodule moved to `contrib/`: unmaintained, not
  built by CI, not published, not referenced by `src/` or `apps/`. What it
  cost is measured: issue #1921 read the Release compile timeline and found
  the vendored tree on the critical path of every build (a 28.3 s window) with
  its **Debug** output landing in the shipped CLI, because the Release build
  produced no Release build of the third-party kit. The product now ships two
  renderers, CellForge and AnsiPlain, and `HARBOR_TUI=nickconsoleex` selects
  nothing. A user who wants SharpConsoleUI clones the tree, builds the wrapper
  and wires it in by hand. This closes one of the three projects in #1921;
  `Harbor.CodeGen` and `apps/Harbor.App.Avalonia` stay open there.
- [ ] **`Harbor.Application` split, variant A, one slice left (ADR-018).** The
  owner decided on 2026-10-16 to decompose `Harbor.Application` (14 areas, 19.5k
  lines; Sessions 44% + Agents 27%) into **five assemblies**, the maximal plan,
  not the incremental `C → B` path the research recommended. Landed:
  `Harbor.AgentRuntime` (#1623, PR #1666), `Harbor.SessionContext` (#1624, PR
  #1714), `Harbor.ChangeTracking` (#1616, PR #1660) and `Harbor.PolicyConfig`
  (#1625 — whose remaining cohort was `Configuration/*` alone, since Permissions
  and Onboarding already left under #1658 and #1701). Open: #1626
  `Intelligence`. Decision, rejected variants, sequencing DAG and the standing
  rules (guard before rewrite; a new axis must be additive and registered):
  [ADR-018](adr/ADR-018-harbor-application-split-variant-a.md).
- [x] `Harbor.Desktop.Abstractions` namespace drift: 4 files declared `namespace Harbor.App.Avalonia.ViewModels` while living in `Harbor.Desktop.Abstractions/ViewModels/`. **Verified fixed (ROP-D Z1, 25.08): every file in the project now declares `Harbor.Desktop.Abstractions.*`.**
- [x] Namespace drift `Harbor.Core.*` in Harbor.Application.dll (42 declarations) and Harbor.Registries.dll (3) — migrated to assembly-matching namespaces (ROP-D Z1). The `Harbor.Core` assembly that inherited the name was deleted in #451.
- [x] Namespace drift `Harbor.Cli.*` in Harbor.App.Cli — 18 declarations + all references migrated to `Harbor.App.Cli.*`; remaining census findings documented as intentional at migration time (compat namespaces in Contracts/Extensions/Registries; same-family sub-namespaces in Ipc/Telemetry/Ui.Framework) (ROP-D Z1, 25.08; see commit 9ec5c7b).
- [x] BannedApi.txt was dead (never wired, wrong filename for the analyzer) — renamed to `BannedSymbols.txt`, wired via AdditionalFiles in Directory.Build.props; all 9 production GetResult sites resolved or pragma-exempted with a catalogued reason (ROP-D Z2, commit be81e42).
- [x] Arch tests probed the wrong assembly for "TuiAbstractions" (typeof(UiStore) from Ui.Framework.State); retargeted to Terminal.Abstractions + new UiFrameworkState rule (ROP-D Z2, commit 9060475).
- [x] ~28 src projects outside arch enforcement → FullLayerMatrixTests covers all 50 in-solution src assemblies (51 in `Harbor.slnx` minus the `Harbor.Plugins.Host` exe; reference check + table guard + exception liveness + coverage guard); stale `dotnetarch.json` deleted in favor of the single enforcement surface (ROP-D Z2, commits 5d2df19/6566be2).
- [x] SystemPromptContext.McpInstructions hardwired null → IMcpRegistry.GetInstructions() aggregates mcp.json hints + initialize responses; WorkspaceContextSource.FormatMcpInstructions feeds the prompt via AgentLoop DI (ROP-D Z3, commit 64cbc0e).
- [x] ResultGuard survived the §4.5 deletion order and gained a new production call (ConfigStore.LoadCore) → deleted as the duplicate canon: ConfigStore load/save and TreeTool now ride CSE `Result.Try` + `ResultErrors.Message` (save path no longer masks OCE); tests ported to ResultErrorsTests (ROP-D Z3 tail, commit 9e954a5).
- [x] ROP-D final verification (25.08): `Harbor.slnx -c Release` builds with 0 errors; full cycle over all 37 `tests/Harbor.*.Tests` projects — итог 1184 tests: 1176–1178 passed, 6 skipped, 1–2 failed = the two pre-existing Avalonia headless flakes `ChatView_Inflates` / `TryGet_ReturnsNullForUnregistered` (61ee126; flake count varies per run). Re-verified in a fresh ROP-D close-out session: same numbers, both failures confined to the known-flake pair. Enforcement matrix: 50 rows under arch rules; out of scope are `Harbor.CodeGen` (build tool), `Harbor.Plugins.Host` (exe) and the `Providers.Shared` + `Storage.Shared` linked-source folders (commit b62de73).
- [x] ROP-D tail-closure re-verification (25.08, after commit 9e954a5): Release build 0 errors (only pre-existing NU1903/NU1901 NuGet-audit advisories); full cycle over all 37 `tests/Harbor.*.Tests` projects — итог 1188 tests (+4 from ResultGuard→ResultErrors test port): 1180 passed, 6 skipped, 2 failed = the same known Avalonia flake pair only.
- [x] God-object decomposition `Harbor.Application/Agents/AgentLoop.cs`: tool dispatch → `ToolDispatcher` + `IToolDispatcher` seam (parallel / sequential fan-out, permission gating, per-call timeout), transient-failure retry with capped exponential backoff + jitter → `Resilience/RetryPolicy`, usage aggregation + O(1) compaction checks → `TokenTracker`/`ITokenTracker`; streaming buffering lives in `StreamingCoalescer`. All behind DI (`CoreModule`); public `IAgentLoop.RunAsync` contract unchanged (AGENTLOOP-DECOMP, commit 31f8859).
- [x] Circular project reference workaround: resolved by the Ui.Framework split (793c998) — `ICommonConfigModelRefReader` (renamed from `ICommonConfigReader` by #453) lives in the bottom `Harbor.Ui.Framework.Abstractions/Configuration` project (narrow session-bootstrap surface only); `CommonConfigReaderAdapter` projects `ICommonConfigStore` onto it per platform. Merging Desktop.Abstractions into Ui.Framework was rejected (wrong direction); splitting Terminal.Abstractions was rejected (churn without isolation). Recorded in DECISIONS.md ADR-009. #453 closed the audit's duplicate claim: the two contracts are a read/write vs read-only capability split, not one contract twice — the reader now returns `Maybe<ModelRef>` instead of a pair of nullable strings, and `CommonConfigContractRules` is the guard.
- [ ] Pre-existing Avalonia 12 headless test failures: 3 tests (`MarkdownRenderer_SetMarkdown_DoesNotThrow`, `CodeBlock_Default_Code_IsEmpty`, `TypewriterStreamingText_CanSet_Text`) fail with "Stack empty" in `SetInheritanceParent`. Needs investigation — likely an Avalonia.Headless bug.
- [ ] IPC tests: 8/35 failing — timing issues with named-pipe disposal on Linux.
- [ ] **Two live file log sinks, deliberately NOT unified (#558).** `apps/Harbor.App.Cli/Logging/` (hand-rolled `ILoggerProvider`) and `src/Harbor.Logging/LoggerSetup.cs` (Serilog, used by Avalonia) both write `harbor-*.log` into `~/.harbor/logs/`. The issue proposed folding the CLI onto Serilog; that is **refused as out of scope in its own right** — unifying the two survivors is a behaviour change to two log formats, not a duplicate to collapse — and they are two different requirements sharing a goal, not two copies of one behaviour: different level model (`LogLevel` Trace..None vs `LogEventLevel` Verbose..Fatal), different line format, different exception rendering (Serilog writes the full `{Exception}` chain; the hand-rolled provider writes one `Exception:` line plus a single `Inner:` line, so a third-level inner exception is dropped), different retention owner. They are also **app-disjoint** — no process loads both, so no line is ever written twice. What #558 did fix is the third instance: a 474-line copy in `apps/Harbor.App.Avalonia/Logging/` with **zero callers**, deleted, with `FileLogSinkOwnershipRule` in `tests/Harbor.Architecture.Tests/` as the guard. Unifying the two survivors, if ever wanted, is a behaviour change to both log formats and needs its own decision.
- [ ] **Both log sinks sweep the same `harbor-*.log` glob** over `~/.harbor/logs` (`LoggerSetup.CleanupOldLogs` and the CLI's `RollingLogCleaner`), so either can delete the other's files — and Serilog additionally self-trims via `retainedFileCountLimit: 50`, so files can be deleted twice over. Pre-existing, unchanged by #558, recorded rather than fixed silently. Needs one retention owner per directory, or a per-prefix glob.
- [x] **The four legacy flat UI-state records are deleted (#597, closing the #594 item).** #594 deleted the `Harbor.Ui.Framework.Reducers` branch and left these four records behind with no writer in `src/` or `apps/`, deliberately, recording the per-record decision as an open item. #597 took the decision: all four are deleted rather than given a producer, because the live `UiState` already carries every field they had (`ChatDomainState` + `TerminalUiState` replace the flat shape field-for-field) — a producer would have been a second way to say the same thing. Two of the four were not the "just delete the file" shape the item assumed:
  - **`SessionsViewState.cs` also declared `SessionInfo`, which is LIVE** — 9 production sites including a `new SessionInfo(...)` in the CLI's `SessionSwitchManager` and `ChatDomainState.Sessions`. The record was deleted and `SessionInfo` moved to its own file; deleting by path would have taken a live type with it, with every pre-existing gate green.
  - **`ChatViewState.cs` also declared `ChatLineViewModel` and `ToolCallViewModel` in the `State` namespace** — same simple names as the LIVE `Harbor.Ui.Framework.ViewModels` pair that all 20 consumer sites bind to, via aliases or full qualification. Zero sites bound to the State copies. Deleting them removes a duplicate-name collision, which is the #558 failure mode; `LegacyFlatTeaBranchRule` now matches them by (name, namespace) so the live pair can never be condemned with them.
  - `AppState` had two **benchmark** readers (`StateDiffingBenchmark`, `SelectorMemoizationBenchmark`). Both measure real shapes, so both were repointed at `UiState` rather than deleted — the numbers now price the state every renderer actually reads.
  - `ChromeViewState`'s one live reader was a `<see cref>` from `Harbor.Desktop.Abstractions`, rewritten to describe the seam instead of naming a deleted type.

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/E2E_TESTING.md -->

# E2E Testing

End-to-end test framework + per-app E2E test suites for Harbor. This document
describes the framework, what's covered today, how to run the tests, and what
remains on the roadmap (TUI / Avalonia E2E).

---

## 1. Why E2E tests?

Unit tests cover individual classes (`AgentLoop`, `ToolRegistry`,
`OpenAiCompatibleLlmClient`, `JsonlSessionStore`, …). They use stubs for every
external dependency. E2E tests go the other way: they spawn the real app
binary, point it at a real (mock) LLM server, drive it like a user would, and
assert on observed output. The pipeline under test is end-to-end:

```
CLI args → Program.Main → HostBuilder → AgentLoop →
  OpenAiCompatibleLlmClient → (in-process HTTP) → MockLlmServer →
    SSE stream → renderer → Console.Out → captured by CliDriver → assertion
```

A regression in any layer (DI registration, env-var binding, SSE parser,
renderer output) surfaces as an E2E failure, not a misleading unit test pass.

---

## 2. Framework layout

All E2E infrastructure lives in `tests/Harbor.E2E.Framework/`. Test projects
reference the framework + the app under test.

```
tests/Harbor.E2E.Framework/
├── Harbor.E2E.Framework.csproj     # net10.0; IsTestProject=true; no Packable
├── IE2eDriver.cs                   # Common contract: Start/Send/Read/Wait/Stop
├── CliDriver.cs                    # Process.Start-based; for one-shot CLI + Blazor
├── TuiDriver.cs                    # PTY-wrapped; for interactive TUI renderers
├── MockLlmServer.cs                # HttpListener; OpenAI-compatible SSE mock
├── E2eTestBase.cs                  # TUnit base; per-test MockLlmServer + temp HOME
├── HarborAppLocator.cs             # Walk up to repo root; locate dotnet host
├── AnsiStripper.cs                 # ANSI escape remover for TUI screens
├── AnsiTerminalBuffer.cs           # 2D terminal emulator; the screen is read from it
└── GlobalUsings.cs                 # Framework-wide using directives
```

The framework carries **no `[Test]` methods**, and that is a rule rather than a
coincidence. TUnit discovers the test classes of a referenced test project
inside every project that references it, so a `[Test]` method declared here
would run once per referencing project. The framework's own tests live in
`tests/Harbor.E2E.Framework.Tests/`, a project nothing references, so they run
exactly once. `tests/Harbor.Architecture.Tests/TestProjectReferenceRules.cs`
enforces both halves of that rule.

Those tests cover the helpers the other E2E projects depend on at run time:
the ANSI scrubber (`AnsiStripper`) and the 2D terminal emulator
(`AnsiTerminalBuffer`), which is what every PTY scenario in
`Harbor.Tui.CellForge.PtyTests` asserts on. They are pure — no PTY, no display
server, no mock LLM server — so they cost a fraction of a second in the `e2e`
shard.

The framework used to carry `StateTestRunner`, a state-based E2E harness whose
`UiState` factories and text extractor no scenario ever called. Its 26 tests
were green and guarded a helper nobody used, so both the harness and the tests
are gone (issue #1812).

The Avalonia desktop driver is **not** here: it lives with the app it drives,
in `tests/Harbor.E2E.App.Avalonia/HeadlessAvaloniaDriver.cs`, because it needs
`Avalonia.Headless` and drives the app in-process on a dedicated UI thread.
(The framework used to carry a second, speculative `HeadlessAvaloniaDriver`
that drove the app through stdin/stdout — a protocol the Avalonia desktop app
does not speak. It had no callers and was deleted.)

### 2.1 `IE2eDriver` — the common contract

Every driver (CLI, TUI, Avalonia) implements the same 7-method surface so
test code is renderer-agnostic:

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `StartAsync(args, env, ct)` | Spawn the app with given args + env vars |
| `SendInputAsync(input, ct)` | Send raw stdin (CLI REPL or TUI input field) |
| `SendKeyAsync(key, mods, ct)` | Send a logical keystroke (Enter, Esc, F12, …) |
| `ReadScreenAsync(ct)` | Read current screen as plain text (ANSI stripped) |
| `WaitForTextAsync(pattern, timeout, ct)` | Poll screen until pattern appears |
| `WaitForExitAsync(timeout, ct)` | Block until process exits; return exit code |
| `StopAsync(ct)` | Force-kill if running; idempotent |

Plus `IsRunning` and `IAsyncDisposable`.

### 2.2 `CliDriver` — one-shot CLI / Blazor HTTP

Wraps `System.Diagnostics.Process` with redirected stdin/stdout/stderr. Resolves
the built DLL (`bin/Debug/net10.0/Harbor.App.Cli.dll`) and invokes
`dotnet exec <dll> <args>`. Sets the working directory to the project root so
ASP.NET Core apps find their `wwwroot`. Async-drains stdout/stderr into a
`StringBuilder` so the buffer never deadlocks. UTF-8 on both streams so emoji
survive.

### 2.3 `MockLlmServer` — in-process OpenAI-compatible HTTP

`HttpListener`-based. Binds a random localhost port (retries on collision).
Endpoints:

- `POST /chat/completions` and `POST /v1/chat/completions` — streams the canned
  response as `text/event-stream` SSE chunks (4 chars per chunk + final
  `[DONE]`). Each chunk is a real OpenAI-shaped JSON object so the client's
  SSE parser exercises its real code path.
- `GET /models` and `GET /v1/models` — static `{ "object": "list", "data": [...] }`.

`SetResponse(model, text)` configures the canned reply per model.
`SetToolCallResponse(model, toolName, args)` configures a single-tool-call
response (for testing tool loops). `ReceivedRequests` snapshots every request
body so tests can assert on system prompt / model / tool list.

### 2.4 `E2eTestBase` — TUnit base class

`[Before(HookType.Test)]` spins up a fresh `MockLlmServer`, allocates a fresh
temp `$HOME`, and drops a `~/.harbor/providers/mock.json` provider config that
points at the mock server. Also writes `~/.harbor/config.json` with
`onboarded: true` so the CLI doesn't launch the onboarding wizard.

`[After(HookType.Test)]` stops the server and deletes the temp home.

`GetEnv()` returns the standard env-var dict: `HARBOR_MODEL=mock/test-model`,
`MOCK_API_KEY=test-key`, `HARBOR_LOGLEVEL=Warning`, `HARBOR_SKIP_ONBOARDING=1`,
`HOME=<temp>`.

## 4. How to run

### 4.1 Build everything first

E2E tests spawn real `dotnet exec <dll>` subprocesses. The DLLs must exist:

```bash
dotnet build tests/Harbor.E2E.Cli/Harbor.E2E.Cli.csproj
dotnet build contrib/tests/Harbor.E2E.App.Blazor/Harbor.E2E.App.Blazor.csproj   # or: dotnet build contrib/Contrib.slnx
```

Both build commands pull in the framework + app under test as project refs
(the Blazor suite resolves its references inside contrib/).

### 4.2 Run the CLI E2E suite

```bash
dotnet run --project tests/Harbor.E2E.Cli -c Release --no-build -- --minimum-expected-tests 1
```

Expected: 7 tests, none failed. A run that discovers nothing exits non-zero
via `--minimum-expected-tests`, so an empty run cannot be mistaken for a pass.

### 4.3 Run the Blazor E2E suite

This suite lives in `contrib/`, which CI does not build (see `AGENTS.md`
§Project structure), so it is **not** in `Harbor.slnx` and is not part of any
test gate:

```bash
dotnet run --project contrib/tests/Harbor.E2E.App.Blazor -c Release --no-build
```

Expected: 3 tests, none failed.

### 4.4 Filter by Category

All E2E tests are tagged `[Category("E2E")]`. Run only E2E tests within one
project — always one project at a time, as a plain executable (`dotnet test`
is not used here; see
[CONTRIBUTING.md §Why not `dotnet test`](../CONTRIBUTING.md#why-not-dotnet-test)):

```bash
dotnet run --project tests/Harbor.E2E.Cli -c Release --no-build -- \
  --minimum-expected-tests 1 --treenode-filter "/*/*/CliE2ETests/*"
```

### 4.5 Detailed per-test output

```bash
dotnet run --project tests/Harbor.E2E.Cli -c Release --no-build -- \
  --minimum-expected-tests 1 --output Detailed
```

---

## 5. How it works — wiring the mock into the CLI

The Harbor CLI resolves providers from `~/.harbor/providers/*.json`. The
`E2eTestBase.SetupAsync` hook writes a `mock.json` provider config that points
at the in-process `MockLlmServer.BaseUri`:

```json
{
  "id": "mock",
  "displayName": "Mock LLM (E2E)",
  "baseUrl": "http://localhost:54321",
  "apiType": "openai-compatible",
  "authType": "bearer",
  "authEnvVar": "MOCK_API_KEY",
  "models": [{ "id": "test-model", "displayName": "Mock Test Model", ... }]
}
```

Combined with `HARBOR_MODEL=mock/test-model` + `MOCK_API_KEY=test-key` env
vars, the CLI's `HostBuilder` registers the mock provider and the
`OpenAiCompatibleLlmClient` hits the in-process server. The full pipeline is
exercised with zero external dependencies.

---

## 6. Roadmap — TUI E2E

### 6.1 PTY-based TUI E2E — DELIVERED for CellForge

**Status:** ✅ `tests/Harbor.Tui.CellForge.PtyTests/` runs real L2 scenarios: a
`PtyHarness` spawns the CLI as a real process inside a pseudo-terminal and
drives it — launch, submit, kitty-keyboard keys, mouse, paste injection,
resize, Ctrl+C, termios restore, plus golden grid-dump fixtures. Run with:

```bash
dotnet build
dotnet run --project tests/Harbor.Tui.CellForge.PtyTests -c Release --no-build
```

The legacy placeholder suites for the contrib renderers remain at
`contrib/tests/Harbor.E2E.Tui.{SpectreTui,Termina,TerminalGui,RazorConsole}/`
(build via `contrib/Contrib.slnx`). They will not pass in the current sandbox because:

- Those renderers call `Console.ReadKey(true)` in raw mode, which requires a
  real PTY. The sandbox blocks `forkpty`/`openpty` via seccomp.
- `TuiDriver` wraps `script -qfc` on Linux to allocate a PTY, but `script(1)`
  is killed before it can exec the app.
- `E2eTestBase.EnsurePtyAvailable()` guards every TUI test — it logs a `[SKIP]`
  message and the test passes as a no-op when PTY is unavailable.

**To finish (for contrib renderers):**
1. Run in a sandbox with PTY allocation (or use ConPTY on Windows).
2. Replace placeholder tests with real driver scenarios: type a prompt, wait
   for the agent's response to render, assert on the visible screen.
3. Wire tool-call canned responses to exercise the tool-call card UI.

### 6.2 Avalonia desktop E2E — DELIVERED

**Status:** ✅ `tests/Harbor.E2E.App.Avalonia/` is implemented and passing.
7 E2E tests run against the real `Harbor.App.Avalonia` app via
`Avalonia.Headless`'s in-process off-screen software renderer. No `xvfb` or
real X display required — the headless platform renders to an in-memory
bitmap.

**Architecture:**

```
Test thread (TUnit)                 UI thread (dedicated)
─────────────────                   ──────────────────────
[Before(HookType.Test)]
  └─ new HeadlessAvaloniaDriver      static ctor starts UI thread
     └─ InitializeAsync()              └─ UIThreadMain():
         ├─ AppHost.BuildAsync()  ──┐     1. Dispatcher.UIThread  (binds)
         │   (on test thread,        │     2. DispatcherReady.SetResult()
         │    ConfigureAwait(false)) │     3. Dispatcher.UIThread.MainLoop(ct)
         │                           │        └─ pumps jobs forever
         └─ Dispatcher.UIThread  ◀───┘
            .InvokeAsync(setup
              Avalonia app)
                                          
[Test body]
  └─ Driver.ScreenshotAsync("01-...")
       └─ Dispatcher.UIThread.InvokeAsync(() => {
            window.UpdateLayout();
            AvaloniaHeadlessPlatform.ForceRenderTimerTick(3);
            Dispatcher.UIThread.RunJobs();
            var bitmap = window.CaptureRenderedFrame();
            bitmap.Save(fs);  // → ~/.harbor/test-screenshots/01-...png
          }).GetAwaiter().GetResult();
```

**Key design decisions:**

1. **Dedicated UI pump thread.** TUnit runs each test method on a fresh
   threadpool thread, but Avalonia's `Dispatcher` + `Application` are bound
   to ONE thread for the process lifetime. The driver's static constructor
   starts a dedicated background thread that binds the dispatcher to itself
   and enters `Dispatcher.UIThread.MainLoop(ct)`. Test threads then marshal
   all UI access via `Dispatcher.UIThread.InvokeAsync(...)` — the job lands
   in the queue, the UI thread's MainLoop picks it up, runs it, and the
   Task returned by `InvokeAsync` completes. No manual `RunJobs` pumping
   anywhere in test code.

2. **`InvokeAsync` + `GetAwaiter().GetResult()`** for synchronous-style
   access (`FindControlByName`, `FindButtonByText`, `OnUIThread`).
   `DispatcherOperation` doesn't have `ConfigureAwait`, so we block via
   `GetAwaiter().GetResult()`. Safe because the UI thread's MainLoop is
   independent — no deadlock.

3. **`ForceRenderTimerTick`** drives a fresh render pass. The headless
   render timer doesn't fire automatically (no 60Hz vsync), so
   `CaptureRenderedFrame()` returns the LAST rendered bitmap. We tick the
   timer explicitly + call `Dispatcher.UIThread.RunJobs()` to drain the
   queued render job before capturing.

4. **Visual-tree-walking `FindByName`** instead of
   `ControlExtensions.FindControl<T>`. The latter only searches the
   immediate `NameScope` of the control it's called on — it doesn't
   recurse into child `UserControl`s. Since `InputBox` lives inside
   `ChatView.axaml` (a `UserControl` embedded in `MainWindow`), we walk
   the visual tree depth-first and match by `StyledElement.Name`.

5. **`OnUIThread<T>(Func<T>)` helper** for reading dispatcher-affine
   properties (`Button.IsEnabled`, `TextBox.Text`) from the test thread.
   Without this, tests throw `"calling thread cannot access this object
   because a different thread owns it"`.

**Tests (7, all passing):**

| Test | Asserts | Screenshot |
|---|---|---|
| `MainWindow_OpensWithoutCrash` | App boots; `MainWindow` non-null; PNG > 5KB | `01-main-window.png` |
| `Sidebar_ShowsHarborBrand` | "Harbor" appears in the rendered visual tree | `02-brand.png` |
| `ChatInput_AcceptsText` | `InputBox` TextBox accepts typed text; `Text` reflects it | `03-input-typed.png` |
| `SendButton_ExistsAndIsEnabled` | "Send ▶" button found by text; `IsEnabled` true when input non-empty | `04-send-button.png` |
| `SessionSidebar_ShowsSearchBox` | "Search sessions" watermark visible | `05-session-sidebar.png` |
| `StatusBar_ShowsProviderAndModel` | Status bar shows "ollama" (default provider) | `06-status-bar.png` |
| `OnboardingWindow_RendersWelcomeScreen` | Onboarding window renders; "Harbor" in brand header | `07-onboarding.png` |

**How to run:**

```bash
dotnet build tests/Harbor.E2E.App.Avalonia/Harbor.E2E.App.Avalonia.csproj
dotnet run --project tests/Harbor.E2E.App.Avalonia -c Release --no-build -- --minimum-expected-tests 1
ls -la ~/.harbor/test-screenshots/
```

Expected: 7 tests, none failed.
Screenshots at `~/.harbor/test-screenshots/01-main-window.png` through
`07-onboarding.png` — open them in any image viewer to SEE what the UI
looks like without running the app.

**Limitations:**

- The Avalonia.Headless software renderer doesn't always pick up dynamic
  text changes (typed text in a TextBox) in the captured bitmap — the
  `CaptureRenderedFrame()` API returns the last rendered frame, and
  `ForceRenderTimerTick` may not fully flush the text formatter's cached
  text runs. The tests assert on the in-memory `TextBox.Text` property
  (which IS updated correctly) rather than the rendered bitmap pixels.
  Visual review of the PNGs shows the static window chrome (title bar,
  sidebar, status bar) but may not show dynamically typed text.
- Tests are tagged `[NotInParallel]` because the driver mutates `$HOME`
  (process-wide env var) and shares the process-wide Avalonia
  `Application` singleton.
- Each test class pays a one-time ~500ms init cost (builds the DI host +
  Avalonia app). Subsequent tests in the same class reuse the singleton.
- **TwoWay binding race**: the `TextBox.Text ↔ ChatViewModel.InputText`
  binding is eventually-consistent across dispatcher cycles. Tests that
  set `TextBox.Text` and then read it back in SEPARATE `InvokeAsync`
  calls can see the value revert to a previous test's text (a deferred
  `VM→TextBox` binding update lands between the set and the read). The
  fix is to set AND read in the SAME `OnUIThread` call — see
  `ChatInput_AcceptsText` for the pattern.

### 6.3 WPF / MAUI E2E

Out of scope for Linux CI. WPF needs the Windows Desktop runtime; MAUI needs
the maui-tizen workload. Both are skipped at the slnx level on Linux.

---

## 8. State Coverage Matrix

The renderer-agnostic `UiState` snapshot (defined in
`src/Harbor.Ui.Framework/State/UiState.cs`) is the single source of truth that
every interactive renderer projects from. It contains **58 distinct renderable
states** across these dimensions:

- **Chat transcript** (7 `ChatRole` values × line presence)
- **Streaming** (IsStreaming, Active.TextBuffer, Active.ThinkBuffer)
- **Agent lifecycle** (IsAgentRunning, WasRunning, Status: idle/running/compacting/error)
- **Input model** (Text, History, HistoryIndex, slash autocomplete)
- **Focus** (FocusMode: Input/Chat/Panel, FocusedPanelId)
- **Scroll** (ScrollOffset, ViewportLines, TotalLines, ScrollPercent)
- **Panels** (TuiPanelState: Hidden/Visible/Focused/Pinned, PanelSizes, RegisteredPanelIds)
- **Session chrome** (Model, Provider, AgentName, Cost)

The matrix below tracks which states are covered by at least one E2E test
across the 5 test projects. A state is "covered" when a test asserts on the
rendered output (or in-memory property) for that state.

### 8.3 Gaps

The 4 TUI projects now share differentiated state tests (no longer copy-paste).
Critical gaps that have been **addressed** by Tasks 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, 4.2:

- **Streaming** (states 5-7): ✅ Covered by `Streaming_ShowsResponse`, `Chat_ShowStreamingBuffer`, `Chat_ShowThinkingBuffer`.
- **Agent lifecycle** (states 12, 56): ✅ Covered by `AgentRunning_ShowsRunningBanner`, `Chat_ShowCompactionStatus`.
- **Panel interactions** (states 32-40): ✅ Covered by `Alt1_TogglesPanel`, `CtrlTab_CyclesPanelFocus`, `Panel_ToggleVisibility`, `Panel_FocusPanel`.
- **Scroll** (states 41-43): ✅ Covered by `ScrollUp_ScrollsHistory`, `Chat_ScrollHistory`.
- **Input history** (states 27, 29): ✅ Covered by `AltUp_NavigatesInputHistory`, `Input_HistoryNavigation`.
- **Autocomplete** (state 26): ✅ Covered by `Tab_AutocompleteSlashCommand`, `Input_AutocompleteSlashCommand`.
- **Error state** (states 10, 54): ✅ Covered by `ErrorState_ShowsError`, `Chat_ShowErrorState`.
- **Compaction** (states 11, 55): ✅ Covered by `Compaction_ShowsCompactionStatus`, `Chat_ShowCompactionStatus`.
- **Tool call** (state 8): ✅ Covered by `ToolCall_RendersToolCard`, `Chat_ShowToolCallCard`.

**Remaining gaps:**

- **Tool result in transcript** (state 9, 21): No test verifies tool result rendering in the transcript.
- **System/Thinking/Error message types in transcript** (states 18-19, 22): No test for system/thinking/error message roles.
- **Panel pinned** (state 37): No test for persistent panel visibility.
- **Active message with both text + thinking** (state 53): No test for simultaneous streaming + thinking.
- **PanelSizes set** (state 58): No test for custom panel size overrides.
- **Focus=Chat** (state 31): No explicit test for chat owning focus (vs input).
- **Agent name display** (state 49): Partially covered — shows in header but no dedicated assertion.

These remaining gaps are tracked for future work.

---

## 9. Conventions

- **`sealed` classes** for all drivers and the mock server.
- **`ConfigureAwait(false)`** on every await in the framework + tests.
- **XML docs** on every public member of the framework.
- **Deterministic waits**: every "wait for X" uses `WaitForTextAsync` with an
  explicit `TimeSpan` timeout. No `Thread.Sleep` in test bodies.
- **Temp HOME isolation**: each test gets a fresh `~/.harbor/` so concurrent
  test classes don't collide on config files or the mock server port.
- **TUnit `[Category("E2E")]`** on every test class + method for filtering.
- **No network**: every external call (LLM, model list) hits the in-process
  mock. Tests pass offline.

<!-- BEGIN SOURCE: docs/EVALS.md -->

# EVALS — task-solving quality (contour B)

Correctness tests (contour A) prove Harbor honors its contracts. Evals prove
it solves tasks. Different loops, different gates. Related: #40, spec 17 §2.

## v0 runner (`tools/Harbor.Evals`, external, no runtime changes)

Per attempt layout: `results/<batch>/<task>/attempt-N/{workspace,verifier,artifacts}`.

1. Copy fixture → `workspace`; capture initial manifest (path → sha256).
2. Copy `verifier/` aside (never inside workspace).
3. Run Harbor: `dotnet <Cli.dll> ask` with piped prompt, `cwd = workspace`,
   kill process tree on timeout (grace: none in v0 — kill is the boundary).
4. Capture raw stdout/stderr; parse `[marker]` events to `events.jsonl`
   (unknown lines → `parser-diagnostics.json`, never silently dropped).
5. Capture final manifest; run verifier (own timeout).
6. Write `attempt.json` (ids, commit, provider/model, env NAMES only —
   never values/secrets, UTC + durations, exit code, runner version),
   `verification.json`, `verdict.json`, `changes.json`.

## Verdict (never one enum)

- execution: `completed | timed_out | crashed | harness_error`
  (`agent_end` + exit 0 = protocol complete, NOT task solved).
- verification: `pass | fail | error` (exit 0 = verifier ran; checks may fail;
  missing/bad JSON = error).
- task: `solved | failed | inconclusive`.
- constraints: `pass | fail | not_evaluated` (manifest-compared outside:
  `mustRemainUnchanged`, `mustNotCreate`; never trust agent self-report).
- agentClaim: manual in v0 (`success | failure | unknown`); no regex on
  «готово». `falseSuccess` only when explicit success claim + proven failure.

## Metrics (batch summary)

Solved share (timeouts count in denominator; harness errors shown
separately); constraint-pass share + coverage; false-success share;
**full cost to success** (all attempts / successes; unknown cost = null,
never zero); failure classes (`incorrect_change`, `broke_existing`,
`violated_constraint`, `timeout`, `harness_or_crash`, `unknown`).

## CI (`evals` workflow — live signal, never a merge gate)

- Triggers: `workflow_dispatch` (inputs: `attempts`, `tasks`) + weekly
  schedule (Monday 03:00 UTC). No `push`/`pull_request` triggers.
- What it does: builds `apps/Harbor.App.Cli` (Release), then runs
  `dotnet run --project tools/Harbor.Evals -- --tasks evals/tasks
  --profile evals/profiles/local.json`, uploads `evals/results/` as artifact.
- Model key: repository secret **`KILO_API_KEY`**
  (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret,
  value `klo_...`). The workflow reads it as `secrets.KILO_API_KEY` and
  passes it as env `KILO_API_KEY` to the runner (model
  `kilocode/kilo-auto/free`, free tier, no card required). The evals pin deliberately
  differs from the embedded provider default (`tencent/hy3:free` in
  `providers/kilocode.json`); background on the two ids:
  `docs/notes/kilocode-default-model-probe.md`.
- No key → graceful skip (green): the `Check model key` step writes a
  notice + job summary and skips build/run; the run stays green because
  live evals are diagnostic, not a gate. Add the secret by hand to enable
  live baselines.

## Rules

- Verifier prompt never gets verifier feedback (no runner-as-fixer loop).
- Conditions pinned per batch: Harbor commit, provider/model, fixture
  versions, limits, date. Real models are nondeterministic — v0 is
  diagnostic (3 tasks fine), not statistical proof.
- Live-model runs are a signal, not a gate; deterministic scripted-provider
  E2E stays the engineering gate.

## Live-run disclaimer (adopted verbatim, issue #40)

Live evals on a rotating endpoint measure Harbor together with the
provider's current routing policy. Results are diagnostic/descriptive;
single runs and small samples prove neither improvement nor non-regression.
Scripted runs check runtime on a controlled stream but do not replace
measuring the model's task-solving. Interleaved A/B (alternating versions
close in time, randomized order, no cherry-picking, model id recorded,
timeouts counted) only for behavioral changes; no automatic live
non-regression gate.

## Open (v1 / follow-ups, not v0)

- `usage.json` cost wiring (full cost to success stays `unknown` until then).
- Windows verifiers (`task.json → verifier.windows` is empty; Unix only).
- Short-lane timeouts (per-task 240 s, suite deadline 12 min) for live CI.
- v1 plugs the same tasks into RunId/budgets/recovery when Run exists.

name: harbor-dev
